findings.title: Autonomous AI Agents are breaking into hundreds of Online Retailers for $25 a target in an ongoing campaign
findings.summary_md: Gambit Security published research on September 22, 2026, after recovering an attacker's staging server used against online retailers. The operator ran Cairn alongside Hermes and Strix, launching 105 attack projects between September 10 and 15 and compromising at least 27 companies. Gambit accounted for more than 600,000 unexpired credit card records from two victims and card-skimmer scripts on five sites, with activity reaching back to July 2026.

findings.title: Inside Cairn: Open Windows into massive AI-Driven Cyber Operations
findings.summary_md: NorForge published its Cairn investigation on October 19, 2026, after locating more than 20 publicly exposed Cairn control panels likely tied to malicious operations. Using Shodan and Censys, the researchers found panels exposing target details, discovered weaknesses, account secrets and API keys, and in some cases root access to attacker data drops. NorForge also observed apparently legitimate red-team operations exposed the same way, potentially putting their clients at risk.

findings.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant published this report on October 30, 2026. They reported observing threat actors using ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN in incident response engagements since late August 2026, with corroboration from research telemetry. The report describes agents conducting lateral movement, database exploitation and exfiltration preparation, and warns that automated chaining of attack paths changes the defensive problem.

findings.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 published research on November 12, 2026, attributing a Cairn campaign to Chinese-speaking attackers tracked with moderate confidence as CL-STA-1238. Between August and September 2026 the actors ran 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in semiconductor manufacturing, U.S. defense policy and civil society, pairing Cairn with Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek. Ten targets saw unauthorized access or data retrieval, including more than one million personal records at one organization, military and government identities, persistent administrator accounts and modification of a live industry standards ballot.

findings.title: AI hacking tool used in US aerospace sector intrusion, Google says
findings.summary_md: Nextgov reported on November 16, 2026, that Google's threat intelligence arm had disclosed an intrusion in the U.S. aerospace sector involving Cairn. Google did not name the victim, describe data taken or attribute the intrusion to a government, and the findings covered activity observed over the preceding quarter. Nextgov noted Cairn's use alongside ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI, and an FBI advisory on ARTEX posted the preceding Friday.

findings.title: Path traversal in datastore upload endpoints allows arbitrary file write
findings.summary_md: GitHub advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94, published November 18, 2026, documents path traversal in MONAILabel's datastore upload endpoints that allows arbitrary file write. The affected package is monailabel up to and including 0.8.5, and the advisory lists no patched version while pointing to Project MONAI pull request 1915 as the fix. It notes that authentication is disabled by default with MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=False, leaving the endpoints reachable by any network caller in a default deployment.
